L3.01.title: a_e (VCe with a)
L3.01.goal: Read and spell words with the vowel-consonant-e pattern using **a**, where a silent final e makes the vowel "say its name" (/ā/).
L3.01.heartLine: once, only (first two of the 16 Level 3 heart words — canonical schedule teaches 2/lesson through L3.08)

read.A: Jane and Kate are at the lake. / Jane has a cane. / Kate has a cape. / They skate on the lake. / Once, Kate got a cramp. / Jane came and gave Kate a hand. / Kate said, "Thank you, Jane!" / They made a plan to skate again.
read.B: Jake has a case to take to the bank. / He made a plane trip. / At the gate, he got a snack and a cake. / Jake's plane was late, but he was not sad. / He said, "I have cash." / Jake sat and had a nap. / Once the plane came, he got on fast.

L3.02.title: i_e (VCe with i)
L3.02.goal: Read and spell VCe words with **i** (long /ī/).

read.A: Mike has a bike. / He likes to ride it. / Mike and his dog Spike go for a ride. / Once, Mike's bike went flat. / Mike did not stop. / He got off and did a quick fix. / Spike sat still. / "Only a bit," said Mike, and they went back.
read.B: Kate got a bike to save time. / She rides it to her job many times. / At nine, she locks the bike and clocks in. / Once, the bike would not go, and Kate had to get off and push it. / She was not glad, but she did not quit. / Only a quick fix did it, and the next ride was fine.

L3.03.title: o_e, u_e, e_e (VCe with o, u, e)
L3.03.goal: Complete the VCe set — read and spell words with o_e (/ō/), u_e (/o͞o/ or /ū/), and e_e (rare, /ē/).
L3.03.newToday: o_e (home, rope), u_e — two sounds: /o͞o/ (rule, June) and /ū/ (cute, mule); e_e (these, Steve — rare, flag it)

read.A: Steve moved to a home. / It is big, and it has a gate. / Steve rode his bike home and did a jig. / He is very glad. / At home, Steve has a cute pet mule named Duke. / Duke likes a plate of grass. / "This home is very fine," said Steve, and he made a note to tell his pal.
read.B: Steve got home very late from his shift. / His job is to help sick kids, and the shift ran long. / At home, he made a snack and sat next to the stove. / His wife left a note: "I made a plate for you." / Steve smiled. / It was a very long shift, but home felt like a rest at last.

L3.04.title: VCe + the Drop-e Rule
L3.04.goal: Apply the drop-e spelling rule when adding a vowel suffix (-ing, -ed, -er) to a VCe word: hope→hoping.
L3.04.newToday: drop-e rule (spelling rule, no new grapheme)

read.A: Sam is making a kite. / He is using tape and a stick. / Every bit has to be just so. / Sam is smiling at his plan. / Once it is done, Sam is hoping for a fine time. / He is saving his kite for the big game. / "I made this alone," said Sam, very glad.
read.B: At the end of every shift, Kate is closing the shop at nine. / She is checking the till and saving the cash. / Once the till is closed, she is locking every gate. / Kate is not rushing — she likes taking her time. / "I am making it safe," she said, smiling at her plan for a safe close.

L3.05.title: Open Syllables
L3.05.goal: Read single-letter open syllables (he, go, hi, me — a single vowel at the end of a word/syllable says its long sound) and two-syllable open+closed words (ro-bot, mu-sic) using V/CV division.
L3.05.newToday: open syllable long vowels (a e i o u alone at a syllable's end = long)

read.A: We go to spot a tiger. / The tiger is silent as it moves. / Because he had a project, a pupil at his class made a robot tiger. / It has one eye that shines. / "This is a great robot!" said the pupil. / We are so glad we came. / We go home and hum a tune, glad for the tigers.
read.B: Kate got a spot in a great program at her job site. / Because there were big tasks, she and the others made a robot to help. / The program runs a set of steps, silent and fast, no fuss. / "We tested it with one eye on the clock," said Kate. / The robot has done every task well. / Kate is glad she got to do this.

L3.06.title: Y as a Vowel
L3.06.goal: Read words where final **y** acts as a vowel: /ē/ in multisyllable words (happy, funny) and /ī/ in one-syllable words (my, fly, cry).
L3.06.newToday: y = /ē/ (end of longer words), y = /ī/ (end of one-syllable words)

read.A: My puppy is very busy. / He runs and hops in the sun by the shed. / My puppy is funny — when he digs in the mud, he gets sticky and muddy. / "Silly puppy!" I said, and gave him a rub. / We go home, and my puppy is happy because he is with me.
read.B: My shift was very busy, because I ran from the front to the back and did not stop by lunch. / When I got back, there was a note from a happy person: "Thank you, you made me very glad." / I am busy, but I am glad I had a busy, happy shift.

L3.07.title: Soft c, Soft g
L3.07.goal: Read words where c says /s/ (soft c, before e/i/y) and g says /j/ (soft g, before e/i/y), plus the endings -ce, -ge, -dge.
L3.07.newToday: soft c (city, ice), soft g (gem, cage), -ce, -ge, -dge

read.A: In the city, there is a big bridge. / Many people cross it often. / Once, my class went on a trip to visit it, because it is huge and made of stage-like steps. / When we got to the edge, we could spot a huge cage with a pet inside. / "So nice!" said the people, very glad. / We had a fine time at the bridge.
read.B: Since the bridge in the city closed, many people had to change the plan. / Many people came to fix it, page by page of a plan they had made. / "It is a huge job, but it is not a bad job if we take the time to do it well," said the judge. / People are glad the bridge will be fine once it is fixed.

L3.08.title: ar
L3.08.goal: Read and spell words with r-controlled **ar** (/ar/, as in car, farm, start) — the first r-controlled vowel, taught here (matching UFLI/RWI sequencing) before any vowel team so common everyday words stop leaking into earlier lessons.
L3.08.heartLine: whole, earth (last two of the 16 Level 3 heart words — all Level 3 heart words are now taught)

read.A: Sam and his mom go to the farm. / A big, red barn is at the farm. / Sam pets a cute pup and a fat pig. / "A big cart!" said Sam. / He rides in the cart with his mom, because he likes it a lot. / They spot a hen in the yard. / Once they are done, they have a snack of grapes. / Sam has a whole, fine time at the farm.
read.B: Kate got a job at the market. / She helps at a cart that sells fresh grapes and plums. / At nine, she sets up the cart and starts her shift. / "This job is hard, but I like it," said Kate. / She helps many people at the market, because she likes to help. / Once her shift is done, Kate has a snack and a cup of milk. / She has a whole, fine time at the market.

L3.09.title: or, ore
L3.09.goal: Read and spell words with r-controlled **or** (for, corn, short) and **ore** (more, store, before).
L3.09.heartLine: none new — all 16 Level 3 heart words were completed at L3.08; today is decoding-only.

read.A: At the farm, Sam spots a horse. / The horse has a short, dark mane. / "Can I ride the horse?" asked Sam. / "Yes, hold on well," said his mom. / Sam gets on, and the horse trots because he holds on well. / Sam has a fun, short ride. / Once he is done, Sam pets the horse and says, "Thank you." / Sam has a whole, fine time at the farm.
read.B: Kate has a list, so she goes to the store. / She gets corn, milk, and a snack from a stand. / Before she is done, she checks her list. / "I got what I came for," said Kate. / She goes to the front and gets a short line. / She is glad she made a trip to the store, because she got what she came for.

L3.10.title: ai, ay
L3.10.goal: Read and spell the long-a vowel team spelled **ai** (mid-word) and **ay** (end of word).

read.A: It is play day at the park. / When rain starts, the class does not stay in — they play in the rain, and get wet from top to tail! / A snail comes on the wet path. / "There is a snail!" said Sam. / They wait for the rain to stop, then drink cold water and play again.
read.B: Every day, Kate takes the train to her job. / Today, because rain made the stop wet, the train came late. / She had to wait, so she got a cup of hot water and a snack from a stand. / "I will just wait," she said to a man in line. / The train came, and Kate got a spot by chance.

L3.11.title: ee, ea
L3.11.goal: Read and spell the long-e vowel team spelled **ee** and **ea**.

read.A: Sam and his team go to the beach. / When they see a green kite, they find a sweet, clean spot to sit. / "Let's eat lunch by the sea," said Sam. / They read a page and laugh at a funny bit. / A queen bee comes to see the sweet leaf, then goes home. / Sam and his team feel very happy after a fine day.
read.B: Each week, Kate and her team clean the street by the shop. / When they meet at nine, each one has a task. / Kate likes to see the street stay neat when they are done. / "We laugh a lot, but we get the job done," said Kate. / At the end, the team sits and has a sweet snack, glad for a job well done.

L3.12.title: oa, ow, oe
L3.12.goal: Read and spell the long-o vowel team spelled **oa** (mid-word), **ow** (often end-word), and **oe** (rare, end-word).

read.A: Sam and his dad walk to the pond with a fine boat. / When snow starts, the pond starts to glow white. / Because it is chilly, Sam puts on his coat and gets a snack of toast. / "Let's float the boat and see if it can go," said Dad. / The boat does float, and Sam claps and laughs. / They walk home, glad they came to play.
read.B: Kate had to walk home since the road was slow with traffic. / She put on her coat, since it was chilly, and got a snack of toast at a stand. / Another man said, "This road is always slow at this time." / Kate did not mind — she got to see the snow glow as she walked. / By the time she got home, she felt glad.

L3.13.title: igh, ie
L3.13.goal: Read and spell the long-i vowel team spelled **igh** and **ie**.

read.A: At night, Sam and his mom talk and gaze up at the sky. / Because the sky is bright, it glows white and high. / "Let's stay up a bit," said Mom. / They eat a slice of pie and talk of the sky. / Sam feels glad for this quiet, bright night with his mom.
read.B: After a long shift, Kate and her friend Jane talk it over at night. / When they sit and gaze up, the sky is bright. / "I might take the job at another site," said Kate. / Jane said, "That is a big thing — talk to your team, then decide." / They eat a slice of pie and talk until it gets late.

L3.14.title: ue, ew, ui
L3.14.goal: Read and spell the vowel teams **ue**, **ew**, and **ui**, which usually say /o͞o/ (as in "moon") and sometimes /ū/ (as in "cute").

read.A: Sam and his mom go to buy a new bike. / "I want the blue one," said Sam. / The shop has a big, blue bike that is true to what Sam likes. / Sam's mom said, "Let's buy it, then get a snack." / They get a bag of fruit and chew on it as they walk home with the new bike.
read.B: Because she had a big meeting, Kate had to buy a new suit. / She went to a shop and got a blue suit that fit true to size. / "This one is right for you," said the person at the shop. / Kate said, "That is true, I will buy this one." / She got a snack of fruit on her way home, glad to have a new suit for the big day.

L3.15.title: oo (Flex-Decoding Two Sounds)
L3.15.goal: Read words spelled with **oo**, which has two common sounds — /o͞o/ (moon) and /o͝o/ (book) — using an explicit flex-decode routine: try one sound, then the other, and check which gives a real word.

read.A: At night, Sam and his dad look up at the moon. / "It is a good, cool night to look at the moon," said Dad. / They sit and look for as long as they can, because the moon is so bright. / Sam has a thing to think of: "What is the moon made of?" / Dad said, "That is a good thing to think of — let's find the answer in a book." / They read a book and find the answer, glad they took the time to look.
read.B: After her shift, Kate likes to sit in her room and read a good book. / When it is cool at night, she gets a hot cup and takes a look at her book. / She took a class once on this same topic, but a book gives her time to think it over. / "I find the answer to a lot of things in a good book," she said. / Soon, she is deep in the pages, glad for a quiet night.

L3.16.title: -ild, -ind, -old, -ost
L3.16.goal: Read words ending in **-ild, -ind, -old, -ost**, a small set of closed-syllable-*looking* words where the vowel is actually long, not short.
L3.16.heartLine: none new — all 16 Level 3 heart words were completed at L3.08; today is decoding-only.

read.A: It is a wild, cold day, and Sam and his mom go for a walk. / They see a child with a gold kite, and the wind is strong. / "Hold my hand," said Mom, "because the wind is wild today." / Sam is glad she told him to hold on. / They walk the whole way home, and Sam feels most glad once they are back and warm.
read.B: Kate lost her old job when the shop closed, so she must find a new one. / Because she is bold, she does not quit — she sends her whole plan to ten shops. / One shop gets back to her and gives her a spot to start. / "I am so glad I did not lose hope," said Kate, most glad to have a new start. / Kate holds on to the good news the whole day.

L3.17.title: Level 3 Review
L3.17.goal: Consolidate all Level 3 code (VCe for all 5 vowels, drop-e, open syllables, y-as-vowel, soft c/g, ai/ay, ee/ea, oa/ow/oe, igh/ie, ue/ew/ui, oo-flex, -ild/-ind/-old/-ost) and all 16 Level 3 heart words before the mastery check.
L3.17.heartLine: all 16 Level 3 words (once, only, very, every, great, eye, busy, people, water, laugh, walk, talk, buy, answer, whole, earth)

read.A: Once, Sam and his family took a whole day just for fun. / At home, Sam ate a bowl of oats and a slice of toast. / Then they went to see a tiger and a robot at a big show. / Sam's eye spotted a huge, gold kite flying high in the sky. / "How very great!" said Sam, and his mom gave him a hug. / Next, they got a snack — a bag of fruit and a sweet, cold treat. / While busy people were there too, Sam felt happy and free. / They went home and read a good book close by the tree. / "This was the best day," said Sam. / His mom said, "I am very glad, too." / They ate a bite of pie, and Sam fell asleep, smiling, once his whole busy, great day was done.
read.B: Once, Kate had a whole day off, and she made the most of it. / She woke up, made a cup of tea, and ate a slice of toast. / At nine, she met her team to help clean up the street — a job she likes since it feels like a great use of a free day. / By noon, the whole team had made the place look neat, and people walking by said, "How nice!" / Kate felt very glad and a bit sleepy, but in a good way. / She got a snack of fruit and a cold drink, then sat and read a good book. / "Today was busy, but it was a great day," said Kate. / Once the sun set, she felt so glad she had spent her whole day well.

L3.18.title: Level 3 Mastery Check
L3.18.goal: Administer the graded Level 3 exit assessment and decide: advance to Level 4, or return to a specific lesson for reteaching.
L3.18.newToday: none — this is the assessment session
